headline: Chips Lead a Fractured Session as Declining Names Outnumber Advancers
body_html:
Tuesday's midday tape is anything but tidy. With 288 names lower against 252 higher across our 544-stock universe, sellers hold a slim numerical edge even as the headline sector — Semiconductors — pushes up 1.34%, offering the session's clearest point of strength. Industrials are adding a modest 0.29% in sympathy, while Healthcare is barely unchanged at 0.01%.

The dominant theme is selectivity. Bloom Energy is the standout mover, surging 8.72% amid apparent interest in alternative power infrastructure, a trade echoed by Primoris Services (+7.04%) and Forgent Power Solutions (+4.95%). On the equipment side, Onto Innovation and Applied Materials are each up better than 4%, lending the semiconductor complex additional support. Fair Isaac is the session's sharpest casualty, off nearly 20% and dragging Financial-Data into the red; Boot Barn, Verra Mobility, and Alpha Metallurgical Resources are also under meaningful pressure.

Into the close, watch whether the semiconductor bid holds or fades as Software — the week's weakest large sector at -0.89% — threatens to drag the broader tape lower. Energy's -0.70% decline adds a cautionary note on commodity-linked names heading into the final hours.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac Craters Nearly 20%, Steepest Single-Name Loss of the Day
briefs.body: Fair Isaac is suffering the session's most severe selloff, down 19.9% at midday and drawing attention across financial-data names. No sector peer has come close to matching that decline. The move is amplifying caution in corners of the market tied to consumer credit analytics and pricing software.

briefs.headline: Bond Market Braces for a New Rate Regime as Opportunity Window Widens
briefs.body: Fixed-income strategists are flagging what they describe as a generational entry point for bonds, with investors who have avoided diversification now facing a compelling case to reconsider. The battered bond market is girding for a structurally higher interest-rate environment, a shift that could reshape multi-asset allocation decisions for years ahead.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Equipment Names Emerge as the Session's Pocket of Consensus
briefs.body: Onto Innovation and Applied Materials are each advancing more than 4%, lifting the broader Semiconductors sector to a 1.34% gain — the best showing among all eight tracked groups. The equipment cluster is attracting buyers even as the wider Software cohort slides 0.89%, underscoring the bifurcation running through Tuesday's technology trade.

briefs.headline: Iran Diplomacy Swirls as White House Distances Itself from Sanctions Relief Reports
briefs.body: The White House pushed back on reports it had proposed easing sanctions in exchange for nuclear concessions from Tehran, while Iranian officials signaled openness to discussions. The back-and-forth follows news that U.S. forces have completed their withdrawal from Iraq after two decades, a development that geopolitical analysts say opens fresh influence avenues for Iran in the region.

briefs.headline: Longevity Medicine Draws Ultra-Wealthy Clientele at Six-Figure Annual Price Tags
briefs.body: A cohort of affluent Americans is committing as much as $250,000 annually to personalized longevity-care programs, according to fresh reporting. Physicians caution that the clinical evidence supporting many of these protocols remains limited, even as demand continues to climb and dedicated longevity clinics expand their premium offerings.

briefs.headline: Indian Rupee Slips Past Key 96-per-Dollar Level on Oil Anxiety
briefs.body: The Indian rupee fell to its weakest level in two months on Tuesday, breaching the psychologically significant 96-per-dollar threshold as concerns about rising crude-oil costs weighed on the currency. The move adds pressure to emerging-market sentiment at a moment when Energy stocks in our universe are already declining 0.70% on the session.
